title: Contract provenance & signing harness for API contract migrations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight contract provenance and signing harness that sits in front of our deprecation/migration orchestration to: (1) cryptographically sign exported API contract snapshots (streaming semantics, function/tool-call schemas, structured-output schemas) to provide immutable provenance for compatibility tests and replay; (2) produce a canonical contract catalog used by canaries and shadow-rollouts to validate behavior-flag migrations; (3) expose an API for downstream test runners and SDKs to verify which contract version and signing key were used for a given replayed request. This work ties together runtime trace capture, contract extractor tooling, CI replay runners, and the migration guide generator.
acceptance_criteria: Contract extractor can snapshot the live streaming/toolcall/structured-output schema and produce a canonical JSON contract file with stable identifiers
Snapshot artifacts are signed with a rotating signing key; verification API returns signer id and signature validity
CI replay job can fetch a signed contract and run deterministic backward-compatibility replay against two runtime versions, passing or failing with an actionable diff report
Migration guide generator consumes signed contract diffs and emits a human-readable migration checklist with suggested behavior-flag toggles and a minimal example
Telemetry events for replay success/failure and signature verification are emitted to the compatibility dashboard
Rolling canary uses contract catalog to gate candidate runtime if contract mismatches exceed threshold
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Patel: Kickoff notes — scope focused on streaming + toolcall + structured-output contracts. Important: signer rotation policy needs to align with Dedicated private deployments' key management.

2025-02-25 - Lina Gomez: Spike complete — prototype extractor for streaming prefixes and toolcall arg schemas. Found edge case where function-calling metadata gets lost when clients use 'partial streaming' mode; captured sample trace and created minimal repro.

2025-02-27 - Michael Cortez (review): Suggested we include a 'compatibility-level' tag in contract snapshots (strict/compat/experimental) to simplify canary gating. Also asked for explicit test vectors per contract.
2025-03-01 - Security (J. Wu): Reviewed signing approach; asked for KMS-backed key storage for Private deployments and HSM support for enterprise. Security review requested (ticket updated).

notes_for_engineering: Implementation components: extractor (runtime hook to emit contract snapshots), signer service (KMS-backed, rotation policy), verification API, CI replay runner integration, migration generator (markdown output), observability events (replay.result, signature.verify). Keep contract format stable and documented in RFC. Add integration tests that run in CI matrix across streaming vs non-streaming clients and toolcall variants.
qa_plan: Add unit tests for contract extractor with synthetic traces (edge cases for partial streaming and large KV cache hits)
Create CI matrix job that pulls a signed contract from artifacts and replays 1000 recorded requests against next runtime image
Failure mode tests: mismatched schema should produce deterministic diff and block canary; signature expiry should surface explicit error and not silently pass
Manual verification checklist for PM/SEs to validate migration guide examples before public docs publish
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signed contracts could leak sensitive prompt text — Mitigation: redaction step before snapshotting and a per-catalog policy to exclude PII fields
Risk: Signing key mismanagement in Private deployments — Mitigation: KMS/HSM integration and customer option to bring-your-own-key
Risk: Replay nondeterminism due to runtime entropy — Mitigation: add deterministic replay mode (seeded RNG, fixed KV state) and mark non-deterministic tests as advisory
